summary: This Standards Track document defines version 2.0 of JSContact, which makes the uid property of a Card optional instead of mandatory. Everything else stays as in RFC 9553. It updates RFC 9555 on converting uid to and from vCard, and registers the vCard JSCOMPS parameter with IANA.

plainLanguage.summary: A digital contact card no longer has to carry a unique ID number. Everything else about it stays the same.

questions: how to convert vcard without uid to jscontact
subtitle: JSContact 2.0 makes the uid of a contact card optional, so cards without a unique ID are valid.

tldr.problem: JSContact required every Card to have a uid, but vCard treats its UID as optional. Converting a vCard with no UID forced implementations to invent an identifier that could differ from run to run.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9982 redefines the uid property of a Card as optional and calls the result version 2.0. All other definitions of version 1.0 stay as in RFC 9553.
tldr.outcome: A Card without a uid is valid in version 2.0, but it cannot be named as a group member or in a relatedTo relation. The RFC also updates the vCard conversion rule from RFC 9555.

today: RFC 9982 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2026. It updates RFC 9555 and has not been obsoleted or updated by another RFC.

sections.title: Why uid Became Optional
sections.content:
In JSContact (RFC 9553) the uid property of a Card was mandatory. In vCard (RFC 6350) the matching UID property is optional. One stated goal of JSContact is to be compatible with vCard semantics, so this difference on such a common element was a mismatch.

Some protocols also do not need it. Address book synchronization protocols such as CardDAV and JMAP for Contacts require the uid, but RDAP has no use for it. The RFC says JSContact should not make protocols generate unique identifiers when they are irrelevant or even detrimental.
sections.plainLanguage: Some contact cards do not need a name tag number, but the old rules made everyone add one anyway. That was like forcing every library book to have a second barcode nobody scans.

sections.title: Version 2.0 and the Redefined uid
sections.content:
The only change is the type signature of uid: it goes from String (mandatory) to String (optional). Because this changes what a valid Card is, the major version of JSContact changes, and this document defines version 2.0.

The RFC adds one paragraph to the property: a Card without a uid cannot be referred to as a group member in the members property or put in relation to another Card in the relatedTo property.

The vCard UID property is not redefined.
sections.plainLanguage: The only rule that changes is that the ID is optional. A card without an ID just cannot be listed in a group or linked to another card, because nobody could point at it.

sections.title: What Implementations Must Do
sections.content:
Implementations MUST create data that complies with version 2.0 (or some later registered version) and set the version property of the Card to that version. They MUST NOT reject a Card without a uid as invalid, unless another document says otherwise or the Card's version is 1.0.

Any valid version 1.0 Card is also valid under version 2.0, so there is no need to migrate existing JSContact data.
sections.plainLanguage: Old cards still work in the new system, so nobody has to redo their address book. New programs just must not complain about a card that has no ID.

sections.title: Converting vCard Without a UID
sections.content:
This section updates the conversion rule from Section 2.1.1 of RFC 9555. The old rule told implementations to generate an identifier when a vCard had no UID, but it did not require the same value across implementations, or even across repeated conversions of the same Card. A recipient unaware that the value was ephemeral might use it in members or relatedTo of another Card, creating invalid relations.

The new rule has two cases:

  • Converting to version 2.0 or higher: implementations MUST NOT generate a unique identifier for uid.
  • Converting to version 1.0: implementations MUST generate a value, how is implementation-specific, and they SHOULD produce the same value for the same Card each time. Implementations SHOULD NOT convert to version 1.0 Cards at all.
sections.plainLanguage: If a paper card has no ID, the new system leaves the ID blank instead of making up a fake one. A made-up ID could change every time and confuse everyone who wrote it down.

sections.title: IANA Registry Updates
sections.content:
IANA has made three updates:

  • The "JSContact Version" registry gets a record for major version 2, highest minor version 0, referencing RFC 9982.
  • The "JSContact Properties" registry adds a reference to Section 4 of this document for the uid property.
  • The "vCard Parameters" registry gains the JSCOMPS parameter, which was defined in Section 3.3.1 of RFC 9555 but mistakenly never registered.
sections.plainLanguage: A big official list of names got updated: it now knows about version 2.0, and a label that was left off by mistake has been added.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document provides no new security considerations. The security considerations of Section 4 of RFC 9553 apply.
sections.plainLanguage: Making the ID optional does not open any new doors for bad guys, so the old safety rules are enough.

viz.caption: WHAT TO DO WITH A VCARD THAT HAS NO UID

cells: MUST generate a uid (SHOULD NOT convert to 1.0)
